title: Older unsupported releases are violating the MPL 2.0 due to a broken link
body:
### Tested versions - Reproducible in commits in the `master` branch that come before d9005912c17ba75e55eca786eb6e46f12a4c85e4. - Not reproducible in d9005912c17ba75e55eca786eb6e46f12a4c85e4 and commits in the `master` branch that come after that one. As far as I know, this problem only affects old unsupported versions of Godot. Currently supported versions of Godot are fine. I know that bug reports for old unsupported versions are usually considered invalid, but I think that this bug needs to be an exception for that rule. [We’re still distributing old versions of Godot](https://godotengine.org/download/archive/), so we need to comply with the licenses for all third-party components that are included in those old versions of Godot. ### System information NixOS 24.05.6122.080166c15633 ### Issue description [We have to comply with version 2.0 of the Mozilla Public License whenever we distribute `thirdparty/certs/ca-certificates.crt`.](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/b00e1cbf743dcb6a2b7f6bd14e348a1a7cf3d403/COPYRIGHT.txt#L182-L185) `ca-certificates.crt` is generated by a tool that converts a `certdata.txt` file into the `ca-certificates.crt` file. In this situation, [`certdata.txt` is the Source Code Form](https://hg.mozilla.org/releases/mozilla-release/raw-file/b8ea2342548b8571e58f9176d9555ccdb5ec199f/security/nss/lib/ckfw/builtins/certdata.txt) and `ca-certificates.crt` is the Executable Form. (The terms “Source Code Form” and “Executable Form” are defined in [section 1 of the MPL 2.0](https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/MPL/2.0/#definitions)). [Section 3.2 of the MPL 2.0 says (emphasis added):](https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/MPL/2.0/#distribution-of-executable-form)

3.2. Distribution of Executable Form

If You distribute Covered Software in Executable Form then:

  1. such Covered Software must also be made available in Source Code Form, as described in Section 3.1, and You must inform recipients of the Executable Form how they can obtain a copy of such Source Code Form by reasonable means in a timely manner, at a charge no more than the cost of distribution to the recipient; and[…]

This means that whenever we distribute a copy of `ca-certificates.crt`, we have to make sure that we tell people how they can get a copy of the corresponding `certdata.txt` file. At the moment, we do that by [including a link to the ca-bundle repo in `thirdparty/README.md`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/tree/b00e1cbf743dcb6a2b7f6bd14e348a1a7cf3d403/thirdparty/README.md#certs). The way that we do it at the moment is totally fine. --- Some old versions of Godot used a different link. Instead of linking to the ca-bundle repo, [some old versions of Godot include this link](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/688228030850005f84d7b51a527bc779d76b905e/thirdparty/README.md#certs): > - Upstream: Mozilla, via https://apps.fedoraproject.org/packages/ca-certificates That link 404s at the moment. The correct new link is . This means that we’re accidentally violating the MPL 2.0. We’re distributing copies of `ca-certificates.crt` without telling people how they can get the corresponding `certdata.txt`. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Change directory into a clone of the Godot repo: ```bash cd ``` 2. Switch to a commit that comes before d9005912c17ba75e55eca786eb6e46f12a4c85e4: ```bash git switch --detach d9005912c17ba75e55eca786eb6e46f12a4c85e4^ ``` 3. Open `thirdparty/README.md`. 4. Find the “certs” heading. 5. Try opening the link to the Fedora ca-certificates package. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A
